titel: Bonus: How 3 Writers Found a Clear Path Through All the Writing Advice

einzeiler: Three writers share how a structured framework helped them finally finish their novels.
kurzfassung: Three authors share their struggles with overlearning, endless line editing, and getting stuck in the middle of their novels. They explain how joining a structured course provided them with the clarity and process needed to outline and write with confidence. Host Savannah Gilbo highlights the difference between merely consuming writing advice and having a reliable system for your story.
stichpunkte: Josie spent a year gathering notes and studying plotting methods before realizing she needed a structured process.
Josie benefited from focusing on her antagonist and theme before building her scene-by-scene outline.
Emily spent her writing time falling down internet rabbit holes and reading craft books instead of making progress.
Emily broke through her stagnation after her husband reframed writing as an investment in her joy.
Nepher spent five years trapped in a cycle of line editing rather than addressing developmental edits.
Nepher learned to align internal and external genres and build meaningful crisis points for her fantasy story.

clips.hook: Overlearning and DIYing an outline from a mess of notes
clips.text: The speaker describes coming from an academic background that led to chronic overlearning, collecting massive amounts of notes, and trying to stitch together various plotting methods independently.

clips.hook: When research and podcasts replace actual writing
clips.text: Instead of working on the manuscript, writing time was consumed by listening to podcasts, reading craft books, and going down research rabbit holes out of a stubborn desire for self-reliance.

clips.hook: Setting arbitrary deadlines and feeling guilty about failing
clips.text: The speaker admits to setting unrealistic writing deadlines without knowing how to achieve them, which resulted in self-doubt and guilt about falling short of creative dreams.

clips.hook: Trapped in a five-year cycle of endless line editing
clips.text: Working on a fantasy project for half a decade got derailed by constantly line editing instead of tackling larger structural story problems.

clips.hook: Why individual writing tips only take you so far
clips.text: The host points out that while craft advice is useful, isolated tips are insufficient without an overarching process to guide a specific story from start to finish.

beschreibung:
If you’ve read the craft books, listened to hundreds of podcast episodes, and studied all kinds of writing advice—but still sit down at your desk wondering, okay, what am I actually supposed to work on today?—this episode is for you.
Because at some point, learning more about writing stops being the missing piece. You need a process that helps you figure out what your specific story needs, what to work on next, and how all the pieces fit together.
In this bonus episode, you’ll hear from three writers who had spent a lot of time learning about writing, but still struggled to turn everything they’d learned into a clear path forward.
You’ll hear from Josie, a self-described chronic over-learner who had studied every major plotting method but kept running into dead ends while trying to outline her novel. Emily, who wrote 35,000 words of her romantic fantasy before getting stuck in a middle she couldn’t see clearly. And Nefer, who spent five years caught in a cycle of line editing when she knew her manuscript needed much bigger changes.
Three writers, stuck in three completely different ways.
But what got all of them moving forward again was the same thing—and it wasn't more craft advice. It was having a process that helped them figure out what their specific story needed, what to work on next, and how all the pieces fit together.
In this episode, you'll hear:
[03:29] How one writer went from cobbling together different plotting methods and running into dead ends to creating a detailed scene-by-scene outline she could confidently write from.
[08:02] How one writer who stalled at 35,000 words finally gained clarity on the entire shape of her story—including the middle that had felt impossibly murky.
[12:33] What happened when one writer zoomed out of her line-by-line prose to focus on the big picture of her story first—and how doing so gave her the clarity to move forward.
If you've spent months, or even years, learning about the craft but still feel unsure what your novel needs from you next, there's a good chance you'll recognize yourself in at least one of these stories.
And if this episode makes you realize a clear process might be the thing you’ve been missing, Notes to Novel is open for enrollment through September 4th.
It's the same process Josie, Emily, and Nefer used to make the progress you'll hear about today. Inside, I'll help you develop your story's foundation, create your cast of characters, and map your plot into a scene-by-scene outline so you can write your draft with clarity and confidence.
